business: Yu Chun Korean Restaurant (sit-down Korean restaurant known for chik naengmyeon, arrowroot black noodles)
target: Diners near Ala Moana and Waikiki looking for a Korean meal: Japanese tourists who know the Yu Chun name, Honolulu locals, and mainland visitors
where: Honolulu, 1159 Kapiolani Blvd, near Ala Moana Center

behaviours.name: Guidebook follower
behaviours.how: Picks restaurants from Japanese guidebooks, blogs and Instagram; Yu Chun is a known name.

behaviours.name: Naengmyeon regular
behaviours.how: Craves cold noodles, comes back every few weeks, especially on hot days.

behaviours.name: Reads every review
behaviours.how: Checks Google and Yelp ratings and recent photos before going anywhere.

behaviours.name: Price-conscious
behaviours.how: Compares menu prices, feels Hawaii prices plus tax and tip add up fast.

behaviours.name: Group dinner organiser
behaviours.how: Books for family or friends, orders sets and BBQ to share.

behaviours.name: Loyal to another Korean spot
behaviours.how: Has a go-to Korean place on Keeaumoku St and rarely switches.

behaviours.name: Adventurous eater
behaviours.how: Wants the dish they cannot get at home, will try the unusual item.

objections: Almost $19 for a bowl of cold noodles feels high, before tax and tip
I can get naengmyeon cheaper on Keeaumoku St
Is black arrowroot noodle really different from regular naengmyeon?
Cold noodles alone won't fill me up, I'd need to add a main
Parking near Kapiolani is a hassle
I've heard the Japanese branches are just as good, so why go here
Service charge on bigger groups makes it pricier

you shop at Ala Moana Center on weekends
you eat Korean food at least twice a month
you look for cold dishes when it is hot out
you are on a budget trip and track every meal
